analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Distributed/Onboarding/ClusterOnboardingLive.swift and the supplied partial patch against the indexed threat model. Lines 912–1333 cover artifact-qualified model choices, private-image labeling, catalog downloads, peer copies and manifest identity checks; no changed behavior is shown there. Lines 1336–1725 cover adoption, draining, coordinator approval attachment, scope changes, local-token forwarding and starts. BASE localRegister (1448–1471) stops/drains parts before approval sync and then calls localServe; BASE serve/localServe (1505–1509, 1681–1698) clear solo state, mark serving and send the peer start. The patch introduces stopsAsked/serveUnlessStopped callbacks (HEAD 77–78), stop counts in follower status (399–408), and a forwarded serve guard (464). These affect A-018 availability and stop/start ordering, with TB-002/TB-011 and T-053 relevant where restarts interact with authorization. Nothing supplied demonstrates an encryption, prompt/cache isolation, attestation, billing or privileged-control regression; T-041 cache internals are not modified in these excerpts.
Integration must examine the omitted HEAD implementations at 1459–1462, 1517–1527 and 1699–1702 together with stop-counter updates elsewhere in this file and the callback consumers. Verify that an intervening stop blocks delayed local and forwarded starts, including registration's restart, and that solo-state clearing does not precede a rejected start. The counter's persistence, comparison and locking semantics are not visible here. The partial patch establishes an intended guard, not its correctness; BASE evidence alone cannot resolve these material lifecycle questions. No supported finding can be attributed to the PR in this scope.
